symptom: QUAL004 reports a microflow started only from the navigation — a profile's home microflow, or a menu item's `call microflow` — as "is not called from anywhere. Remove if unused", while `mxcli refs` lists its `home_page` / `menu_item` edge (ako/mxcli#1484, upstream mendixlabs/mxcli#1579; the 4 NAV_ findings left in ako/mxcli#1639's Formula1Frontend)
cause: The rule decided "has a caller" from its own copy of the reference vocabulary, MICROFLOW_ENTRY_KINDS. The page list (PAGE_ENTRY_KINDS) had `home_page` and `menu_item`; the microflow list did not, though the catalog emits both kinds into a MICROFLOW too (a home microflow, a menu item that calls one)
insight: This was the fourth time the same list fell behind (datasource/action/calculate, schedule, settings/publish, event, now the navigation pair) — **a consumer that keeps a copy of an allowlist of edge kinds will fall behind the producer again**, and the upstream one-line fix (add the two kinds) would have reset the clock. The rule now counts any edge into the document, i.e. the graph `refs` and GRAPH_DEAD_ASSETS already read; no kind targeting a microflow or page means anything but "this runs/opens it", so no exclusion list was needed. Drift is guarded behaviourally rather than by a second list: `catalog.RefKinds` is held complete against the RefKind constants (AST scan), and TestQUAL004CountsEveryRefKind drives every one of them at a microflow, a nanoflow and a page through the real rule, with an unreferenced microflow as the per-kind control — so a new kind is tested the moment it is declared, and a reintroduced allowlist fails by kind name. Verified on a real 11.13 app with the BASELINE binary and only the rule swapped: NAV_Home/NAV_Orders drop out, an unreferenced microflow and page are still reported. The OData microflows in the same report are a catalog gap, not a rule gap: `refs` was empty for them too (ako/mxcli#1639)
